questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stand as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim at the top of the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stand as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stand as far away from the fire as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not the flames. If you are unsure which extinguisher to use, wait for firefighters.

questions.question: Before driving in winter, you should check:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your defrosting and heating equipment, coolant and antifreeze, wipers and washers, tire tread, tire chains, lights, reflectors, and exhaust system. Clear ice and snow from all windows, mirrors, steps, and the radiator.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth must be at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 of an inch tread depth in every major groove. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: You should not back up in a straight line.
You should not correct drift until you are very far off course.
You should pull up to reposition the vehicle as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should pull up to reposition the vehicle as needed.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, pull up to reposition your vehicle as needed.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: Do not engage the parking brake.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block the wheels.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting the engine, engage the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before you enter the cab and start it.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early, well before you turn or change lanes.
Signal continuously until the turn is complete.
Do not signal if no one is near you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not signal if no one is near you.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Signal early and keep signaling throughout your move. Cancel the signal after you are done. Always use your signals.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop shortly to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire is clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: Stop a short distance after changing a tire to recheck the tightness of the lug nuts.

questions.question: Good drivers look ____ seconds ahead of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle if it is moving slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: While any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes.

questions.question: During a vehicle control test, a look is when:

options.text: A driver checks the dashboard gauges.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back to check the vehicle's position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back to check the vehicle's position.
questions.explanation: A look is when you open your door, get out, and walk to the back to check where your vehicle is. You can use one look during straight line backing and two looks during other exercises.

questions.question: When doing a pre-trip inspection, what should you check in the fifth wheel gap?

options.text: There is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
The locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When checking the tractor and trailer connection, look in the fifth wheel gap. Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: When turning left with two left turn lanes available, which lane should you use?

options.text: Trucks should not turn where there are two left turn lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to turn left. When an intersection has two left turn lanes, use the right lane to start your turn.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an upcoming bridge, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down as you approach it. Try to find a different route if possible.

questions.question: If your wheels start to spin when you accelerate on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: If your drive wheels spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, release the accelerator.

questions.question: What should be true about a safety belt?
questions.correctAnswerText: It should latch securely.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, check that the safety belt is securely mounted, adjusts properly, latches securely, and is not ripped or frayed.

questions.question: What is the line that passengers must stand behind on a bus called?
questions.correctAnswerText: The standee line.
questions.explanation: On a bus with standing passengers, no one may stand in front of the rear of the driver's seat. The bus must have a line or marking on the floor showing where passengers cannot stand. This is called the standee line.

questions.question: What can help you avoid becoming drowsy while driving?

options.text: Get about three hours of sleep beforehand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan ahead, including stopping points.
questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue while driving, get seven to eight hours of sleep before your trip, drive during hours when you are normally awake, plan to take breaks, and exercise regularly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of bad brakes?

options.text: Pads free of oil or grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: When checking your brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil, grease, or brake fluid, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn very thin.

questions.question: How should you do a driver's side parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Pass the parking space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the parking space without passing it first.
Back into the parking space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For a parallel parking space on your left, drive past it first. Then back into it, keeping the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: What is the minimum size for hazardous materials placards?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 and three-quarter inches.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.
